newsitem.title: USA: Intel says Digital chip contracts end in Q3. [corrected 15:45 gmt]
newsitem.headline: Intel says Digital chip contracts end in Q3. [corrected 15:45 gmt]

text.p: In an escalation of the patent dispute between Intel Corp and Digital Equipment Corp, Intel said contracts to supply its Pentium family of chips to Digital run out after the third quarter of 1997.

The assertion was made in a May 15 letter by Thomas Dunlap, Intel's chief legal counsel, addressed to Thomas Siekman, Digital's chief legal counsel, that was filed as part of an Intel suit alleging breach of contract by Digital.
In the letter, Dunlap (Corrects from Siekman) said his company took issue with recent statements by Digital officials that it has "long-standing supply agreements with Intel."

Digital officials made the comment two weeks ago in the course of announcing a patent infringement suit against Intel alleging that Intel had misappropriated patented technologies used in Digital Alpha chips for use in Intel's Pentium family.

In a letter dated May 20, Digital responded to Intel by saying that Digital has had a direct purchasing relationship with Intel for more than two decades and that it had extended its purchasing agreement last year until June 30, 1999.
But an Intel spokesman said Wednesday his company continues to believe that its contracts to supply Pentiums to Digital only extend through the third quarter of this year.

In addition, Intel spokesman Howard High said Intel is seeking the return immediately all of the information, including proprietary microprocessor specifications and product prototypes, that Intel has supplied Digital.

In the May 20 letter, Siekman complained that Intel had cancelled meetings with its PC engineers and was demanding the return of Intel briefing materials related to the upcoming relase of a new chip code-named Deschutes.

In the letter, the Digital official said both companies would be hurt if Intel materials were withheld from Digital, a move that would prevent Digital from releasing on schedule a new line of PCs based on the Intel Deschutes chips.

The letter said the Maynard, Mass.-based computer maker sought to keep its dispute versus Intel limited to a technology dispute and not to have it spill over to affect Digital's "commercial" ties to Intel.

While both Digital and Intel supply microprocessors chips, Digital's Alpha chips are largely used in powerful business and research computers. By contrast, Intel is the world's dominant supplier of chips used in a range personal computers.
As such, Intel supplies Pentium microprocessors used in a broad line of Digital personal computers.
